visual: Pale sky reserves the upper field for black bold sans. The person and cars occupy the lower half. A red underline marks the starting-over premise; the final concession reverses to white type on black with a red phrase.
story: Acknowledges audience skepticism and proposes putting ability to a test. Opens the question of what the test will involve.
lesson: The concession makes the next promise relevant. Use an actual buyer objection and a credible demonstration; Pulsify should replace the lifestyle backdrop with work-based authority.

visual: Retains B1's photo and opening text. Additional blocks extend down into the darker trees, changing to white type and black backing. A red circle and long underline emphasize the live, five-day demonstration.
story: Pays off the promised test with a starting-from-zero challenge and a time boundary. Leaves the conditions and viewer participation to follow.
lesson: Progressive addition can create continuity without a new photograph. Keep the added material readable and the original material subordinate enough to avoid a full reread.

visual: A new, darker photo places four cars low and open sky above. Three red X marks create an immediately scannable restriction list. The underlined headline and unfinished last line leave open space below.
story: Removes personal brand, case studies and connections as explanations for the promised success. Ends by signaling an additional condition.
lesson: The visual list is objection handling. Only claim constraints that will actually be honored; the empty lower text area becomes useful space for the next reveal.

visual: Keeps B3's restriction list and scene. Adds a black-backed participation sentence with a red word, a concrete activity list and an underlined closing promise.
story: Moves the viewer from observing the challenge to doing the work alongside the creator. Names outreach, pitching and closing as the activity.
lesson: Explain what participation consists of. This frame's persuasion comes from the added access promise, not additional graphic complexity.

visual: Same scene again, but the restriction block is removed from the top. The participation and activity copy remains, followed by a circled date range and a pale pink event-name backing with red type.
story: Turns the public challenge into a named, dated bootcamp. Resolves when and what the event is.
lesson: Recompose when the information priority changes. Progressive storytelling does not require keeping every old sentence indefinitely. Dates must remain accurate wherever saved.

visual: New photograph of a person reclining on a car. White bold copy fills the quiet upper region; a single red underline introduces the giveaway list. No proof cards or elaborate diagrams.
story: Adds prizes and an in-person dinner as attendance incentives after the main event has been explained.
lesson: Separate the offer's useful promise from bonus incentives when evaluating it. The source does not establish whether these prizes attracted suitable customers.

visual: Retains B6 and adds early-bird pricing in blue, a red-underlined action line, a small capacity statement and a large white native link sticker with blue text.
story: Converts accumulated interest into a ticket purchase. Gives the price, action and claimed urgency on the same frame.
lesson: Price and destination are explicit. The claimed room limit is not verified. Pulsify's current watch-only highlight should not inherit this paid-event close.

visual: Black story field with a single large white ticket link sticker centered vertically. Phone and Instagram chrome remain outside the designed content.
story: Provides a stripped-down repeat of the ticket action in the captured state.
lesson: It may be a deliberate action reset, but a still cannot rule out missing or loading media. Do not infer its duration, click rate or surrounding motion.

visual: Two columns: numerous small gray price tiles versus fewer larger mustard tiles. Thin white tile edges distinguish overlap. Serif setup, heavy sans headline with red underline, and color-matched bullet descriptions sit above two people at a table.
story: Advocates a higher-price, lower-volume offer by contrasting workload, buyer characteristics and fulfillment room.
lesson: Count, size, color and copy reinforce one comparison. Abstract shapes are clearly present. The arithmetic is approximate: seven $14K offers total $98K, not $100K.

visual: Profile identity at top; a zigzag timeline connects warm yellow through orange, red and pink dots. Dates and large amounts flank message crops. The gym subject overlaps middle cards; the final message is enlarged with a white circle and serif teaser.
story: Presents a named client's progression after joining, then announces an interview for deeper evidence.
lesson: Attach identity, period and supporting artifacts to a result path. The linking layout suggests progression but does not independently verify the amounts or causal contribution.

visual: A large three-band teal funnel overlays architecture, with outlined stage labels on the left and thin connectors. Bands lighten downward and extend beyond the right edge. Angled content-thumbnail tiles occupy the bottom foreground.
story: Names the Profile Funnel and maps different content/advertising activities to stages after the client progression.
lesson: Meaningful abstract geometry belongs in the vocabulary. Its area is conceptual, not measured. Preserve complete essential labels even when an oversized figure bleeds off the frame.

visual: Three differently sized chat receipts over a cabin photo. The middle panel passes behind the person's head and body. Large extracted amounts sit beside the corresponding panels, with red underlines and smaller qualifiers.
story: Broadens credibility through several client-result claims rather than another explanation of the mechanism.
lesson: Subject overlap creates depth while external callouts keep the result readable. Preserve the distinction between a day total, paid-in-full amount and offer value.

visual: Abrupt change to a bright payment screen. Black-backed white text surrounds a large daily earnings figure. The DM keyword appears in its own block, with a follow-up explanation of fit.
story: Uses a source-presented earnings screen, a target customer situation and a scaling promise to lead into a personal reply invitation.
lesson: Changing from cinematic scenes to a plain receipt shifts attention. The ambitious timeline and competitive claims remain unverified; explicit fit language is more transferable than those promises.

visual: Warm architectural scene with blue windows. Large white mechanism headline sits mid-frame, underlined in blue. The smaller teaser ends behind the person's head while the main headline stays clear.
story: Uses a familiar named method as the reference point for a larger coming reveal.
lesson: This is a direct text-behind-subject example. Its depth is attractive, but the hidden ending is also a readability cost. Protect essential words in Pulsify.

visual: White product recommendation card above centered explanation; large red-underlined data word; a dimmer follower card appears lower over a dark car scene. Brightness separates primary and supporting UI.
story: Introduces data as the claimed answer to predictability and shows a recommendation before explaining the full product.
lesson: A concrete output can establish usefulness before a feature list. The product recommendation and projected impact are source claims, not demonstrated results from this screenshot.

visual: Photo of a person presenting to a group. A short two-line heading sits above the screen, with the product category bold and underlined red. Screen content is indistinct; most of the image is allowed to breathe.
story: Introduces a claimed nine-month build and ends with an unfinished feature-list setup.
lesson: The room and gesture establish a demonstration scene. The following frames need to complete the setup; production duration alone is not evidence of utility.

visual: Same presentation scene. Enlarged UI follows the screen plane behind the presenter. A three-node blue line lights the first node. On the right: white number badge, blue-backed explanation and a serif consequence line.
story: Feature one claims automatic tracking across the advertising-to-return path, with manual-work relief beneath.
lesson: Screen, gesture, progress and copy act as one demonstration. Reproduce the relationship with verified product behavior; do not infer the original editing software.

visual: Scene and layout persist; the middle progress node lights. Screen shows cost and conversion overview cards. The right-side badge advances to two, with a concise explanation and serif line about scattered sheets.
story: Feature two moves from data collection to seeing the connected overview.
lesson: Advance both the information and the progress state. The same photo is purposeful because the viewer stays inside one explanation.

visual: Third node lights and badge advances to three. Product recommendation UI replaces the overview on the screen; text and the pointing person retain their established positions.
story: Feature three moves from visibility to a recommended next action, then promises less guesswork.
lesson: The collection-to-overview-to-action order makes the product easier to understand. Claims of expert-level speed and revenue impact need separate substantiation.

visual: Warm hotel scene. Short authority statement above a serif aside; two bullet paragraphs grouped by a thin red rectangular outline. Bold phrases identify scale, duration and refinement work.
story: Attempts to justify why the product's knowledge and claimed results are difficult to reproduce.
lesson: An outline can group evidence without turning it into a generic card. It supports hierarchy; it does not turn claims of spend and returns into verified evidence.

visual: White headline over stairway photo. Three transformation lines emphasize the desired terms in red blocks. A right-hand vertical stack of recognizable platform/service marks is connected with plus signs.
story: Summarizes the claimed before/after benefit and connects the product to a familiar tool environment.
lesson: Red here emphasizes positive outcomes, contradicting a red-means-pain-only rule. Preserve only verified integrations and avoid importing the unsupported return multiplier.

visual: Two profile states occupy opposite ends of a blue rising line with nodes. Red annotation frames counts and points toward a large softened video thumbnail. An underlined watch prompt and native link complete the route.
story: Packages audience-growth claims into a deeper video with a specific reason to watch.
lesson: Profiles can become endpoints in a visual argument. The line has no readable data scale. The headline says 91,500 while the shown profile says 91.1K; explain dates or reconcile figures.

visual: White screen, short black title and one horizontal wallet crop with several brightly colored balance panels. Large unused space surrounds the source UI.
story: Returns to a routine-results/status message after the video-routing frame.
lesson: This is a separate proof-like punctuation frame, not another feature demonstration. Pending and available balances must not be combined or called daily revenue without evidence.

visual: A grid of content captures fills the background. View counts are circled red. A much larger purple-lit foreground portrait overlaps the grid; the headline stays high and clear.
story: Advocates a niche audience with buyers while showing a body of content and its visible attention counts.
lesson: The archive wall communicates accumulated work. Visible views do not prove the buyers claim. Pulsify can show its own backtrackable work without borrowing status imagery.

visual: Six frosted rounded tiles in a three-by-two grid, bright edge treatment, concise claims and smaller qualifiers. Below, a white arrow leads to a bright daily earnings crop over the same portrait scene.
story: Expands the claimed business model into economics, team size, client intake and payment behavior, then adds a daily receipt.
lesson: A card grid works here because the items are parallel descriptors. It would be the wrong default for a story with one developing thought. All business figures remain source claims.

visual: An enlarged dimmed Instagram profile is the background. White stage labels and red curved arrows connect areas down toward a visible video thumbnail card. The native profile remains recognizable.
story: Demonstrates a route through the creator's content/profile assets into a deeper video.
lesson: Annotate the real interface rather than drawing generic boxes for everything. These stage labels express this source's model and should not be transplanted as universal funnel definitions.

visual: Plain dark canvas. Three spaced centered sentences compare the same amount across year, month and day. One wide message crop supplies a named source and differentiates generated revenue from collected cash.
story: Uses time compression to heighten a client-result claim after the content-system explanation.
lesson: Type alone can carry a strong comparison. Preserve the message's metric distinction; generated revenue and cash collected are not interchangeable.

visual: Bright architectural photo with a small person at the window. A white revenue-chart crop sits high. Three bold white-on-black copy groups compare two Decembers and announce ten lessons.
story: Introduces a before/after transformation, a source-presented result and a finite learning promise together.
lesson: A long sequence benefits from a clear contract. The chart has visible dates and a label, but is still not independent verification of the business claim.

visual: Restaurant scene with pink architectural lighting. Black close-fitting text backing creates separate groups for lesson title, concessions, claimed missing capability, quotation and takeaway.
story: Lesson one reframes attention toward buyer quality rather than engagement alone.
lesson: Grouped text exposes the argument even on a busy photograph. The claim about earning with a small audience is source assertion; the visual is atmosphere, not evidence of audience quality.

visual: Black field, white headline box with a red word, two profile screenshots, green check/underline for the preferred method, red X/underline for the before state, and a blue upward arrow.
story: Offers a same-account follower comparison immediately after the audience-quality lesson.
lesson: Identity continuity makes comparison legible. Counts support a change in followers, not the qualification or causal claims added in the surrounding copy.

visual: Warm ornate lounge; text groups occupy the upper portion above the seated person. A repeated lesson/concession/gap/principle layout creates familiarity.
story: Lesson two introduces predictable acquisition as the next missing capability.
lesson: The recurring frame lets the changing problem lead. A daily qualified-follower promise requires operational evidence beyond an attractive scene.

visual: Dim follower-notification feed as background; bright header box; red enclosure around ad spend; small source chart; a vertical set of bold white funnel figures with final revenue breakdown.
story: Follows predictability with the densest account of spend, stages and collected amounts in this set.
lesson: Give a result its denominator and path. The three money components reconcile to the total, but call-completed versus show-up definitions and source currency need clarification before using ratios.

visual: High viewpoint into a bright apartment with a small standing figure. Bold white text in black backing stays above the person; the same lesson grouping continues.
story: Lesson three moves from attracting leads to the need for someone to turn conversations into meetings.
lesson: Advance to the next bottleneck created by the previous capability. The delegation principle is attributed teaching, not a literal universal performance rule.

visual: Nighttime group dinner. Four widely spaced black-backed statements occupy the dark upper area, leaving the social activity visible below.
story: Presents hiring spend, applications, hires and subsequent impact as an example following the delegation lesson.
lesson: People imagery can make a team discussion human. The photo does not establish each person's employment, the hiring numbers or the stated financial impact.

visual: Night street scene. White text is set directly into the dark upper field. A purple character is visibly integrated with the car lower down beside the person.
story: Lesson four identifies incomplete funnel visibility, while introducing a recurring product motif before its explicit explanation.
lesson: Brand foreshadowing can happen inside the scene. The image establishes a visible motif, not the exact method used to create it or the cost of hidden funnel losses.

visual: Stage photograph with product name and interface imagery on the screen. Copy is divided above and below the presenter, leaving the screen identity and audience visible.
story: Reveals Mochi as the answer to the tracking lesson and lists what it is claimed to monitor.
lesson: Introduce the product after the relevant need. A live-looking presentation establishes context, while the revenue multiplier remains an unverified promise.

visual: Large out-of-focus phone inbox dominates the left foreground. Right-aligned text backing occupies the remaining space over a dark venue scene.
story: Lesson five addresses offer positioning and upfront purchase willingness.
lesson: Alignment responds to the picture instead of a fixed template. Inbox density suggests activity but the blurred messages cannot establish sales, intent or payment amounts.

visual: Dusk villa scene with a lone laptop user below. Several text groups sit over dark sky/architecture; the lower warm-lit scene stays visible.
story: Lesson six distinguishes headline revenue from take-home profit and advocates low expenses.
lesson: The wealth-coded setting can create tension with the expense message. Do not infer ownership or costs; use directly relevant work evidence for Pulsify's version.

visual: Sunset exterior with a laptop large in the foreground, a small walking person mid-distance and black-backed lesson copy high left.
story: Lesson seven shifts from competing on quality toward harder-to-copy identity and delivery.
lesson: Foreground, middle ground and horizon create depth without composited UI. The specific time-to-copy threshold is the source's rhetoric, not a measured competitive law.

visual: Airline cabin objects fill the scene. Black-backed paragraphs leave the laptop and headphones visible. No graph or proof card is needed for the explanatory passage.
story: Lesson eight argues for agreement between words and visuals.
lesson: Apply the congruence principle to real work and real claims. The source's absolute statement about friction and sales should not become a guaranteed commercial law.

visual: Open vehicle storage area with several purple character plush figures and a silver case. Short lesson lines with black backing occupy the upper region.
story: Lesson nine advocates concentrating on the few tasks claimed to produce most results, while repeating the product character in physical form.
lesson: A brand object can recur playfully without a repeated corner badge. The numeric productivity split is a rhetorical illustration, not demonstrated time-study data.

visual: Wide podcast studio scene with lights and microphones. Right-aligned text groups use the upper-right field while both seated people remain visible below.
story: Lesson ten argues that useful offers and results still need visibility. Completes the promised ten-part set.
lesson: A media scene directly matches a visibility lesson. Preserve that word-image relationship without assuming another creator's set or production level is necessary.

visual: Daylight table scene with two people, foliage and warm natural detail. Black-backed copy continues the established style above them.
story: Packages the preceding lessons into a repeatable process, adds scale claims and addresses relevance across niches before the invitation.
lesson: The softer scene changes the emotional register, but intent is inferred. Do not reuse the universal niche or financial claims without a matching evidence base.

visual: Smiling person holding shopping items in a mall, with several black-backed paragraphs above. The reply keyword sits inside a detailed call invitation rather than a separate huge button.
story: Asks the ready viewer to request a custom roadmap/fit conversation after referencing the results already presented.
lesson: The proposed call has an explicit purpose. The image does not prove the person's role or relationship to the creator. The absence-of-selling language is itself persuasive framing.

visual: Reuses NH2's restaurant photo. Many smaller text-backed groups occupy the upper area, with an additional case claim low down. Visible highlight age changes to 26w.
story: Adds relatability, a model-based explanation, free-help framing, a tomorrow/three-slot invitation and a further case claim.
lesson: A highlight can contain later additions. Exact posting dates and genuine availability are unverified; dated scarcity can become stale in a permanent asset. This frame is notably dense.

visual: Dark studio photo, large red italic emphasis within a white heading, red-underlined amount, white rounded earnings crop and lime arrow. A screen brand remains visible in the room behind the person.
story: Uses an unexpectedly disappointed tone about a claimed strong day to create curiosity for the comparison that follows.
lesson: The next slide must explain the comparison. Tone and evidence are coordinated, but Pulsify should not inherit status-based dissatisfaction as its default voice.

visual: Huge white name, lime amount, smaller time qualifier. White message panel contains a dashboard; a green triangular connector points to a circular enlarged detail with a ring. Small banknote decorations overlap the amount area.
story: Answers S1 with another person's larger claimed day and a source-presented receipt.
lesson: The magnifier makes the decisive detail readable and traceable. Decorative money adds little evidential value. Keep the source's metric label in any enlargement.

visual: Workspace photo, headline and purple hourglass/mechanism emphasis. Two white event cards are stacked, with the person's head/body restored in front of the lower one.
story: Attributes the claimed booking volume to beta access to a named method, then shows created and completed event totals.
lesson: A numeric UI artifact is more concrete than a broad claim, but created events alone do not establish qualified sales calls or causal impact.

visual: Cabin photo with reduced background color. Yellow revenue headline, dark message panel, lime cash callout and curved arrow. The person's colored head overlaps the lower-right part of the receipt.
story: Continues from completed events to a weekly revenue claim while separately calling out collected cash.
lesson: Separate revenue and cash in both wording and display. Keep the figures and qualifiers exposed around the subject overlap.

visual: Mostly grayscale boat scene with a colored foreground person. Huge name, bold result, purple mechanism pill and green arrows above a broad dark message panel that passes behind the subject.
story: Adds another client example linked to the same named method, with a detailed payment-source list in the message.
lesson: This is the clearest selective-color and subject-over-proof example. The payment list sums to its shown total, but is still a source-provided claim. Keep important lines clear of the body.

visual: Garden conversation scene. A short white paragraph with one blue phrase and hand underline sits at top. A round blue tap-hand graphic occupies the lower field.
story: Introduces a week spent implementing the method together and leaves the resulting capabilities unfinished.
lesson: A simple human scene can slow the pace after dense proof. The still establishes a tap prompt, not its actual interactive behavior or animation timing.

visual: Same photo and paragraph as S6. Adds a blue curved arrow and three blue diamond list markers. The lower circular graphic changes to a red heart.
story: Completes the implementation setup with claimed lead flow, pre-sold buyers and clearer scaling decisions.
lesson: The added list is the information change. The word unlimited is an unverified promise; a graphic's change between stills does not establish the exact interaction.

visual: Dark aircraft scene under a complex route: profile/portrait, small cost message, YouTube header, three highlight circles, miniature story captures and a closing DM. Red arrows and brief white labels connect the artifacts.
story: Connects a claimed audience increase to acquisition, nurturing, evidence and a DM purchase path.
lesson: Use actual interface artifacts to explain a journey. Tiny text limits readability, and follower counts do not prove all followers are qualified or ready to buy. No final audience-facing commercial CTA is captured.

visual: Podcast portrait fills the frame. Large white subject introduction with a red name block sits high; a white curved arrow points toward the person. Warm leather, skin and black clothing hold the palette.
story: Introduces the person who will be the subject of a content/funnel breakdown.
lesson: Visible publisher is kobeynguyen, not Shelby Sapp. The arrow's simple job is identification; the picture supplies recognition and a media context.

visual: Retains K1 but dims the existing photo, headline and arrow. A new centered two-line sentence becomes the bright foreground, with its large business claim highlighted red.
story: Adds age and scale to make the subject worth investigating.
lesson: De-emphasizing the prior layer makes the new claim lead without resetting the scene. The number is attributed promotional copy, not an audited valuation or revenue finding.

visual: Subdued sea photograph, centered explanatory copy with red money emphasis, white curved arrow and large rounded thumbnail reusing the podcast portrait and red block treatment.
story: Presents a further scale claim, then offers a bounded eleven-minute video breaking down the funnel and content.
lesson: Show the actual asset and the time commitment. The thumbnail repeats the identity already introduced, making the destination recognizable.

visual: K3's content becomes a dark background. New lower copy leads to a large red reply-keyword block and a smaller white delivery-promise pill.
story: Requests a short keyword reply in exchange for the previously shown video.
lesson: One action and one promised delivery make the exchange clear. The reply route needs a real fulfillment process; the screenshot does not prove an automation exists.
